Purchase order: Your written agreement to buy specific pieces from a supplier.
Goods receipt: A record of the good and damaged pieces that actually arrived.
Supplier invoice: The supplier’s bill for the pieces and charges supplied.
統一發票: Taiwan’s official tax invoice. Keep its number and original evidence.
Landed cost: What stock cost to reach you, including the eligible inbound charges.
WAC: Weighted average cost: total sellable stock value divided by its pieces.
COGS: The stock cost used up when you dispatch an order.
Deferred revenue: Money received before dispatch; it is not yet earned sales.
Accrual: A cost already incurred whose bill has not arrived yet.
Reversal: A new opposite entry. The original record remains unchanged.
Trial balance: A list of account balances used to check the books.
Period close: Locking a month after all five evidence checks pass.
